name: PlayStation 4
description: shadPS4's own options, then the settings given to Box64 before every PS4 game starts on the phone — shadPS4 is x86-64 code that Box64 translates. The server runs it natively and ignores the Box64 ones.

sound.label: Sound
sound.description: The session's sound through the phone, or nothing: the emulator still decodes audio, but SDL plays none of it — a little lighter.

pipelineCache.label: Pipeline cache
pipelineCache.description: shadPS4 keeps the GPU pipelines it compiles, and reuses them at the next start instead of compiling them again: a shorter start, fewer stutters the first time a scene appears. The first game still compiles everything once.

turnipDebug.label: Adreno driver workaround (Turnip)
turnipDebug.description: A debug option of Turnip, the graphics driver of Adreno phones: it changes how the driver renders, to work around its bugs. For a game whose log ends with “Device lost” — Final Fantasy VII Remake on the S25 (2026-10-26). It has no effect on another graphics processor.

options.flushall: flushall — empty the GPU caches after every draw (slower)
options.syncdraw: syncdraw — one draw at a time (slow)

dynarec.label: Translator (DynaRec)
dynarec.description: Box64 translates the game's x86-64 code into ARM code. Off, it interprets it instead: many times slower, but exact — the way to tell a translation fault from the game's own.

cpuType.label: CPU shown to the game
cpuType.description: The processor Box64 tells shadPS4 and the game it runs on. The PS4's is an AMD one: told an Intel without SSE4a (Box64's own default), shadPS4 rewrites thousands of the game's instructions, and scans the whole game for them at every start — 108 s of the start of Final Fantasy VII Remake on the S25 (2026-10-26).

trustShared.label: Game code in shared memory
trustShared.description: shadPS4 maps all the game's memory, its code included, from one shared file. Box64 cannot see a write made to that code through another view of the file, so on its own it checks every piece of the game's code it translated each time it runs it: 62 % of the processor time of Final Fantasy VII Remake on the S25 (2026-10-27). On, Box64 protects that code like ordinary memory and checks it only after a write. A PS4 game never writes its own code.

strongMemory.label: Memory ordering
strongMemory.description: How faithfully the translator keeps the x86 memory ordering, which ARM relaxes. Stricter is slower; “Strong” is the usual fix for a multithreaded program that misbehaves.

safeFlags.label: Flags safety
safeFlags.description: How carefully the translator preserves the x86 flags across calls and returns. Box64 ships with 1; the PS4 needs 2 on the phone — with 1, a “rep cmps” given a zero count loses the flags of the instruction before it, so the games' own memcmp compares wrong, and Final Fantasy VII Remake dies at its start (2026-10-26). The PS5 needs 2 too, and it costs nothing measurable there.

bigBlock.label: Block size
bigBlock.description: How much code the translator handles in one block. Smaller blocks are slower but closer to the x86 instruction by instruction.

callRet.label: Call/return optimisation
callRet.description: A shortcut for the x86 call and return instructions. Off is the safest, and on the phone the fastest to start: with Default, Kingdom Hearts III shows its first picture after 159 s, against 42 s with Off (Melody of Memory 123 s against 18 s, 2026-10-27), for the same frame rate afterwards.

fastNaN.label: Fast NaN
fastNaN.description: Skips the exact propagation of NaN values in floating-point maths. Off is exact and slower.

fastRound.label: Fast rounding
fastRound.description: How the translator rounds floating-point results.

x87Double.label: x87 precision
x87Double.description: The precision of the legacy x87 floating-point unit.

alignedAtomics.label: Aligned atomics
alignedAtomics.description: Treats the x86 atomic operations as aligned. Off is the default.

nativeFlags.label: Native flags
nativeFlags.description: Uses the ARM flags to compute the x86 ones. Off is slower and exact.

selfTest.label: Translator self-test
selfTest.description: Runs every instruction through the interpreter as well and reports the first difference. Extremely slow: diagnostics only.

log.label: Box64 log
log.description: How much Box64 writes to the game's log.
